data.exact_reserve_text: In 2016, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m (2015: GBP 27.1m) due primarily to a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts following lower than expected incurred claims movements during 2016 and a release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account as policies come off risk.

prior_year_events.event_name: International cat events (Chile, NZ, Japan, Thailand)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Gross incurred losses from the international cat events of GBP 25.5m with a further provision of GBP 3.6m; IBNR remains on Japan and Thailand after settlement on NZ exposure.

Expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account is GBP 88.5m, of which GBP 69.6m had been incurred at year end; continued caution on potential development of flood losses in Metropolitan New York.
Reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts leading to a favourable movement (contributed to overall surplus in ultimate claims).

named_events.loss_description: Expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account is GBP 88.5m of which GBP 69.6m had been incurred at year end; cautious evaluation of potential flood losses in Metropolitan New York.

named_events.event_name: International cat events (Chile, New Zealand, Japan, Thailand)
named_events.loss_description: Gross incurred losses from the international cat events of GBP 25.5m with a further provision of GBP 3.6m; only IBNR remains on Japan and Thailand after settlement on NZ exposure.
Lower than expected incurred claims movements during 2016 led to a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts, contributing to a surplus.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2016 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 321.0m. During 2016 there was an overall favourable development (a release) in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m (6.3% of opening gross reserves), driven principally by favourable development on long-tail medical malpractice (casualty) claims and release of catastrophe loadings on prior years (notably affecting property catastrophe exposures). The movement is reflected across older underwriting years (net release), with casualty classes accounting for a large proportion of the back-year release and smaller releases in short-tail catastrophe-exposed property balances.
raw_causal_phrases: overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m (2015: GBP 27.1m)
a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts
a release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account as policies come off risk
The movement in the net provision for claims includes a release of GBP 26.7m in respect of claims outstanding at the previous year end
The long-tail casualty classes account for around 47% of the back-year release

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (liabilities) 2015 comparative. Prior year development used the explicit narrative 'overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m' (stated in notes/claim triangles) as a gross figure (report also provides a net release figure of GBP 26.7m). Claims development triangle is present but includes an aggregate '2010 and prior' column which is excluded from diagonal calculations; some LOB allocations and amounts are inferred from percentage descriptors in the narrative (e.g. '47% of back-year release to long-tail casualty'), so LOB-specific amounts are approximate and carry lower confidence.
